To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the paradoxical effects of antitumor immunological strategies on growing tumors are explained assuming that the tumor-immunological interactions at low stimulatory IR ratios are tumor-promoting.
the tumor-promoting effect of the immune response evoked by tumor vaccines and immune-checkpoint inhibitors can be counteracted by the use of anti-inflammatory strategies and/or p38 inhibitors.

the tumor-immunological therapy-induced IR is not linear but bipasic, with strong IR inducing inhibition and weak IR stimulating tumor growth, which can be counteracted with selective inhibitors of the p38 signaling pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel strategies to counteract the tumor-immunopromoting effect and thus to improve the efficacy of immunological treatments for tumors.
the improvement of antitumor therapies by counteracting the tumor-immunogenic effect.
the identification of the molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in tumor immunostimulation and with the development of new therapeutic strategies based on counteracting tumor-immunostimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tumor immunostimulation, as a phenomenon, is not necessarily a tumor-protective mechanism but rather a tumor-promoting one.

, although tumor-immunostimulation is a general phenomenon that occurs in growing tumors, it is only when immunological therapies are initiated at tumor stages at which tumor growth is stimulated that they are able to enhance tumor growth.

, in general, tumor-inhibitory effects are achieved by the immunological therapies on small-sized tumors while tumor-promoting effects are achieved by those strategies on medium-sized and larger tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

tumor-immunostimulation is the main obstacle to be overcome in order to achieve a successful immunotherapy of growing tumors, and that the most efficient way to overcome this obstacle is by using p38 inhibitors in conjunction with immunological strategies.
the tumor-immunomodulating effect of immunological therapies can be counteracted by anti-inflammatory agents and selective inhibitors of p-38 signaling pathways.

, in the case of immunological therapies for cancer, one should be aware of the possibility that the immune system can act as a double-edged sword, and that, in order to avoid tumor-promotion, the tumor-immunogenicity of the tumor should be counteracted with selective inhibitors of pro-inflammatory signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the therapeutic potential of immunological strategies may be enhanced if the tumor-immunomodulatory effects of these therapies are properly counteracted.
, in order to improve the therapeutic efficacy of immunological strategies, it is essential to counteract the tumor-immunomodulatory effects of tumor growth.
the tumor-immunological therapies should be administered at early stages of tumor growth, where they are expected to inhibit tumor growth.
